description.value: The study examined PTSD-related differences in lateral occipital complex function and occipital gray matter volume in combat veterans using functional MRI and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The current study examined the influence of PTSD on occipital cortex function and volume.

value: We hypothesized that veterans with PTSD would show diminished habituation in the lateral occipital complex to repeated presentation of generally aversive stimuli that is unrelated to their trauma.
We also hypothesized that the severity of symptoms would correlate positively with the lateral occipital complex response to novel, aversive stimuli.
we hypothesized that veterans with PTSD would have reduced gray matter volume in the occipital cortex relative to veterans without PTSD.
We further hypothesized that the severity of symptoms would correlate negatively with occipital gray matter volume in veterans with PTSD.

description.value: Participants viewed aversive and nonaversive images from the International Affective Picture Set in novel and repeated conditions while performing a one-back-matching task.

instructions.value: Participants performed a one-back-matching task throughout the imaging run. For novel pictures, they indicated whether two successive images were identical; for repeated pictures, they indicated whether two successive images had the same contrast.

stimuli.value: Aversive negatively valenced/unpleasant images not related to combat, nonaversive neutral-valence images, and black screens with a fixation cross. Novel epochs contained 11–12 different pictures of the same valence; repeated epochs presented the same picture 15 times.
